justification: All nine conditions required for Gift Aid eligibility on donation FP-0316-EL are satisfied on the evidence supplied. (a1) The charity holds current HMRC recognition confirmed on 16 March 2026. (a2) Elaine Carter is an individual donor paying from a personal current account. (a3) Total Gift Aid recoverable on all her donations in the tax year to 5 April 2026 is £80, well below the £980 Income Tax she paid, satisfying E04/E07. (a4) She signed an electronic Gift Aid declaration on 15 March 2026 explicitly covering this donation, matched to FP-0316-EL. (a5) The payment did not go through Payroll Giving. (a6) No goods or services are linked to the payment. (a7) No benefit beyond a standard thank-you email was provided. (a8) No shares or other assets were delivered. (a9) FP-0316-EL is a direct Faster Payment from Elaine's bank on 16 March 2026, clearly distinct from the CAF card and voucher redemptions (CC-0314, VC-0317) batched on 18 March; it is not a charity-card or voucher donation. The treasurer may therefore include FP-0316-EL in the ordinary Gift Aid return.
scope_issues: This assessment covers only transaction FP-0316-EL. Monthly direct debit donations and other one-off donations must each be assessed separately against the same conditions.

The policy passages do not specify whether an electronic Gift Aid declaration satisfies E05; the scenario treats it as valid but the passages are silent on acceptable formats. On the facts as presented no disqualifying defect is identified.

The tax-paid condition (a3) is assessed on the figures provided for Elaine Carter only; if other charities are also claiming Gift Aid on her donations in the same tax year and those claims are not reflected in the £80 total, the aggregate comparison could differ, though the scenario gives no indication of such additional claims.
